newsitem.title: UK: World LPG prices weaken, Euro propane sheds $100.
newsitem.headline: World LPG prices weaken, Euro propane sheds $100.

text.p: International Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) prices extended losses this week, but few deals were heard in Europe and Asia as buyers held back in anticipation of further falls, traders said.
European propane prices plummeted, with large cargoes bid as low as $245/$250 a tonne cif Rotterdam, a loss of over $100 a tonne on the previous week.
"Propane's falling out of bed," said one dealer.
Sea-going coasters were talked as low as $290/$300 a tonne fob U.K.
Traders said that propane prices were speeding towards "cracking levels" -- the point at which the product could be used as a petrochemical feedstock.
The cracking level was pegged around $10 to $20 below naphtha prices, which were close to $230 a tonne cif on Friday.
"The cracking level will provide a natural floor (for propane)...at that point a lot of new buyers will come in," said one northern European trader.
Butane, the traditional petrochemical feedstock, eased slightly in Europe this week with cargoes traded at $240/$250 a tonne cif Rotterdam, and $245 fob Sullom Voe.
In the Mediterranean, propane also softened, with ample supplies seen across the region for the second half of February. Bids slid by some $40 to $50 a tonne to around the $300 mark.
Butane held firm however, with healthy buying interest reported. A small cargo traded at $283 a tonne fob Lavera.
In East of Suez markets, buyers stuck firmly to the sidelines, holding out for a lower benchmark Saudi contract price (CP) in March.
The Gulf fob market slipped with prices pegged at a $10-$15 discount to the CP.
"It's Chinese New Year and nothing is moving to Japan or South Korea anyway," said one trader active in the Far East market. "They're determined not to buy until March."
Premiums were notionally assessed at CP +25 cents C+F Japan and Korea.
Bidders for Abu Dhabi's selling tender for end-March loading propane and butane cargoes were seen scarce.
"The way the market is at the moment, there's not much interest," said one trader.
The tender for 31,500 tonnes of propane and 13,500 tonnes of butane for loading March 26-28 is scheduled to close on February 11.
U.S. propane also softened this week, flying in the face of bullish weekly data which showed a 2.3 million barrel draw on inventories.
Prices at the spot the Mont Belvieu trading hub in Texas slipped by some 3-4 cents to 36/37 cents a gallon by the end of the week.
--Rosalind Russell, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5387
